question.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]t{e}^{4t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ b\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =4$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}4-4 & 5 \\ 0 & 4-4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5{w}_{2}=1 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{2}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{1}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{1}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{4t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=0,b=\frac{1}{5},$ and $a+b=\frac{1}{5}.$
